Either wire `removeFiles` into the cleanup flow (perhaps as a fallback) or remove it to keep the build clean.

🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. Inline comments: In `@src/commands/actions/download_boot_artifacts_cmd.go`: - Around line 110-113: The call to the shell builtin is using util.Execute which invokes exec.Command and will fail; replace the util.Execute("unset container") invocation with util.ExecuteShell("unset container") so the command runs in a shell (mirror the retry path), updating the call that assigns stdout, stderr, exitCode (and any error handling) in download_boot_artifacts_cmd.go to use util.ExecuteShell instead of util.Execute. - Around line 107-109: The short declaration in the syscall.Mount call shadows the outer err; change the `if err := syscall.Mount(sysrootFolder, sysrootFolder, "", syscall.MS_REMOUNT, ""); err != nil { ... }` to assign into the existing error variable (e.g. `err = syscall.Mount(...)` then `if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf(...) }`) or use a distinct name like `mountErr` so the outer `err` is not shadowed; keep the fmt.Errorf call unchanged but reference the non-shadowing error variable. - Around line 80-89: The run() loop currently swallows all errors and always returns nil; update it so that it returns the last non-nil error from runDownloadBootArtifacts when all retryCmdAmount attempts fail, and avoid calling time.Sleep(defaultCmdRetryDelay) after the final attempt. Specifically, track the error returned by runDownloadBootArtifacts inside the loop (referencing runDownloadBootArtifacts, retryCmdAmount, defaultCmdRetryDelay), only sleep when i < retryCmdAmount-1, and after the loop return the recorded error instead of nil so callers can detect failure. - Around line 114-123: Replace the ineffectual re-assignment of stdout with _ when running util.ExecutePrivileged("rpm-ostree", "cleanup", "--os=rhcos", "-r") before checking exitCode, and restructure the logging so success messages are only emitted on successful exit codes: call util.ExecutePrivileged once, if exitCode != 0 call util.ExecuteShell("unset container") and retry (assigning to _, stderr, exitCode), then if the retry exitCode == 0 call log.Infof("Successfully removed rhcos") else call log.Errorf with both stdout and stderr from the failed attempt(s) using their respective variables (and avoid printing unconditional success messages); reference variables stdout, stderr, exitCode and functions util.ExecutePrivileged, util.ExecuteShell, log.Errorf, log.Infof to locate the code to change. - Around line 241-247: getSize currently uses os.Stat(folder).Size() which returns directory inode size (~4KB) and causes cleanup to always run; replace its implementation to call syscall.Statfs (or unix.Statfs on non-deprecated platform package) for the mount containing folder and compute available bytes as stat.Bavail * uint64(stat.Bsize) (convert to int64) so getSize(folder) returns real available filesystem bytes; update error handling to wrap syscall failures and keep the same function signature so callers like getSize (used by the free-space check) get correct values. --- Nitpick comments: In `@src/commands/actions/download_boot_artifacts_cmd.go`: - Around line 249-263: remove the dead helper or wire it as a fallback: either delete the removeFiles(folder string) function entirely, or call it where filePath is constructed (use the same filePath variable) as a cleanup fallback when the rpm-ostree cleanup path fails; if choosing the fallback, invoke removeFiles(filePath) in the error branch after rpm-ostree returns an error and log any error returned from removeFiles; ensure references to removeFiles, filePath and rpm-ostree are updated accordingly and handle/propagate errors consistently. ```
